## A Ship for All Destinations

_aka, "Destination Everywhere"; aka, "An Anchor in Time"_

**Javier Ontiveros** + **San Jaya Prime**

  

This one is near 'n dear to my heart. It's the one and only collaboration I ever made alongside my master -- the man who taught me fractals and how to seamlessly blend them with real-world (and completely surreal) elements... Javier Ontiveros, aka "Fucking Batoruco."

  

His original joke about the piece was that the ship was undeniably beautiful to look at, but it unfortunately sank entirely due to its design. But that "sinking" part -- combined with the shape itself -- sparked an idea. What if the ship was both vessel and anchor? Not only does it physically look like an anchor, but I started building a whole mythos around it in my head... a ship that moves through time and space using mass-distortion, effectively anchoring itself into a completely different reality.

  

_A new ship was born._

  

* * *

  

My final version has prints and more [here on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23979379). You'll find Javier's original version [here on DeviantArt](https://www.deviantart.com/j-a-v-i-e-r/art/A-Ship-For-All-Destinations-24832381).

texts:
## An Anchor in Time

If you look closely, the mass generator is the square at the very top of the anchor. Near that generator, I twisted the clouds, using Mandelbrot spirals to make them even more torrid and chaotic the closer they get to the core.

  

I re-textured and completely redesigned the intricate details of the ship, though I barely touched the core form. Mostly, I extended the rigging so it fully connected all the moving parts, then detailed the surrounding areas with heavy hooks and braces.

  

Where the ship stretches the farthest outward, bending into spirals, the geometry becomes smaller and smaller... literally stretching out of our current dimension. The ship is actually constantly anchored across five spatial dimensions and one temporal dimension. Those curled hooks? They're used to "anchor into" a different dimension whenever the vessel's mass distorts across space.

  

I’ll eventually be writing a short story to go along with this design, diving into the initial discovery of the vessel and how they slowly uncovered its insane navigation capabilities.

  

For now, here it floats in an eternal sunset. The waves crash around it, slowly causing the vessel to bob up and down... yet it moves no farther nor nearer to the shore. It just remains here, waiting until it's called to move.

  

Until then, you can check out the alternate fractal planet version I made for the design -- the "Steampunk Spelljammer" -- down below.

texts:
## Legacy of the Symbol Fractal

After Batoruco's passing, both Aftermath Arts and myself picked up the "symbol fractal" method he’d originally taught us. We updated the technique to work in modern versions of Apophysis -- which remains one of the most incredible fractal flame apps ever created (You can see my blue glass "[Symbol of Purpose](dharmamix)" right here on this site in the section on [DharmaMix](dharmamix)). To this day, I still teach other budding fractalists how to create symbol fractals using this exact method in Chaotica and other flame-iterative apps. For those who use Apophysis, you can find the most up-to-date version that I've created [here on DeviantArt](https://www.deviantart.com/jayaprime/art/Apophysis-Script-Batoruco-s-Symbol-v4-0-582725379).

  

Javier's art, and his discoveries, live on.

  

_<font face="Times New Roman">**Batoruco** -- aka, "The Crazy Old Man" (February 14, 1952 - July 31st, 2009)</font>_

  

## The Last Laugh

You thought you'd be forgotten old man. Well... joke's on you! I took the planet from "Spelljammer" with our ship, then worked it into my "[Celestial Return](celestial-return)" mural. Now thousands and thousands see it as it travels between festivals and at Burning Man every year. _Good luck trying to be forgotten! And you better be laughing wherever you are._
